name: University of British Columbia
summary: The University of British Columbia is a public research university with two main campuses, Vancouver and Okanagan (Kelowna). This record covers the Vancouver campus: the BA in Economics (Vancouver School of Economics) and the BSc in Computer Science (Faculty of Science; students enter Science first and then enter Computer Science).

totalStudents.notes: UBC-wide headcount (both campuses), undergraduate and graduate, per the 2025/26 Annual Enrolment Report; read via search excerpt because the PDF host was not fetchable.

undergraduates.notes: Search excerpt of the 2025/26 Annual Enrolment Report gives undergraduate enrolment of 59,688; verify against the report.

internationalShare.notes: Report excerpt: international students are 25% of the total student population (18,009 students) and 25% of Vancouver undergraduates.

applicationPlatform.value: UBC online application (apply directly to UBC)

applicationFee.value: CAD 173.25 for international applicants who require a study permit (non-refundable)
applicationFee.notes: Taken from a search excerpt of the official Dates and deadlines/application pages.

testing.notes: Optional for applicants following the US curriculum; applicants are not disadvantaged for not submitting.

english.waiver: UBC lists nine ways to meet the English Language Admission Standard, including four or more consecutive years of full-time English-medium education immediately before UBC in Canada or in a country where English is the principal language.

internationalTuition.notes: Vancouver campus, 30 credits/year: Faculty of Arts CAD 51,530.40 (CAD 1,717.68 per credit); Faculty of Science CAD 53,082.00 (CAD 1,769.40 per credit). Excludes non-instructional fees. Tuition for students starting in 2026/27 may rise by up to 3% per year; 2027-28 rates for the 2027 intake were not confirmed.

scholarships.name: International Major Entrance Scholarship (IMES)
scholarships.eligibility: New international undergraduate students on a Canadian study permit who apply by the international admissions deadline are automatically considered; based on outstanding academic achievement.

scholarships.name: Outstanding International Student Award (OIS)
scholarships.eligibility: New to UBC, entering from secondary school or post-secondary on a Canadian study permit; outstanding academic achievement and strong extracurricular involvement. Applicants who apply by the deadline are automatically considered.

scholarships.name: UBC International Scholars Program
scholarships.eligibility: Need-based program for international students with exceptional academics and leadership and significant financial need; separate award application required.
scholarships.coverage: Up to the full cost of the academic program and living expenses, based on individual financial need assessment

deadlines.label: Application deadline, Winter Session 2027/28 (international applicants consideration for International Scholars awards)
Document deadline for out-of-country post-secondary applicants

opportunities.name: Computer Science Co-op Program
opportunities.description: Salaried work terms of 8-20 months depending on program; BSc, BA or BCom students majoring in Computer Science can apply from the second term of first year after completing CPSC 110, 121 and 210 (or in progress).

opportunities.name: Undergraduate Student Research Awards (USRA/SURE) in Computer Science
opportunities.description: Summer research awards fund 16 weeks of full-time work in a department lab; SURE is open to domestic and international students.

opportunities.name: Data Science for Social Good (DSSG)
opportunities.description: Interdisciplinary summer research program on data-intensive projects open to full-time UBC students with 75 completed credits; eligible for Science and Arts Co-op credit.

programs.name: Economics (BA), Vancouver School of Economics
programs.school: Vancouver School of Economics (Faculty of Arts)
programs.summary: Students enter the Faculty of Arts and then the Vancouver School of Economics after completing prerequisites: a differential calculus course, ECON_V 101 and ECON_V 102, selected options and a writing course (27 credits in total).

requirements.minimum: IB Diploma with at least 24 points including bonus points is the general minimum; a higher score is required for most programs (UBC does not publish a specific figure in the retrieved pages)

subjects.subject: IB English A (Language and Literature or Literature)
Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches (satisfies Pre-Calculus 12 equivalent for economics)
subjects.notes: Applications and Interpretations HL also accepted; Applications and Interpretations SL and Math Studies do not satisfy the math requirement for the Vancouver School of Economics.

subjects.subject: Any academic subjects
subjects.notes: Standing in at least six academic subject areas (GCSE, AS and A level) with at least three academic A levels or six AS levels.

requirements.notes: UBC encourages but does not require A levels in subject areas related to the intended study. Program-specific A-level mathematics requirement for Economics was not found; Pre-Calculus 12 equivalence is applied as for other curricula.

subjects.subject: Senior English
subjects.notes: General minimum final grade of 70% in junior or senior English for English-medium schools.

subjects.subject: Mathematics (Pre-Calculus 12 equivalent for Economics)
subjects.notes: UBC states program requirements for Canadian applicants are applied as appropriate to international curricula; exact Indian-board subject lists are determined by UBC Admissions.

requirements.notes: Schools affiliated with CBSE; overall minimum admission average 70%. UBC publishes no fixed Indian-board subject list; evaluation is by UBC Admissions.
Schools affiliated with CISCE (ISC). Subject-by-subject Indian requirements are not published; assessed by UBC Admissions.

subjects.subject: AP English Language and Composition (English 12 equivalent)

requirements.notes: UBC grade conversion for admission: AP 5 = 96%, 4 = 86%, 3 = 80%, 2 = 70%. First-year credit generally for AP grade 4 or better in equivalent courses.

subjects.subject: Mathematics
subjects.notes: Three years of mathematics to the junior level; Economics requires Pre-Calculus 12 equivalent.

requirements.notes: Graduation from a regionally accredited US academic/college-prep program; at least six senior-level courses recommended.

programs.name: Computer Science (BSc), Vancouver
programs.school: Faculty of Science (Department of Computer Science)
programs.summary: High-school applicants cannot apply directly to the Department of Computer Science; they enter the Faculty of Science, complete first-year Science, and then apply to the Computer Science program.

requirements.minimum: IB Diploma with at least 24 points including bonus points is the general minimum; a higher score is required for most programs

subjects.subject: IB English A (Language and Literature or Literature)
Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.notes: Applications and Interpretations HL also accepted; Applications and Interpretations SL and Math Studies are not acceptable.

subjects.subject: Biology, Chemistry or Physics
subjects.notes: One of the three is required, plus Grade 11 or equivalent Chemistry and Physics.

requirements.notes: UBC's general IB requirement also refers to a completed Diploma including at least three Higher Level courses.

subjects.subject: Mathematics (Pre-Calculus 12 equivalent)
subjects.notes: Science program prerequisites for Canadian applicants (Pre-Calculus 12; one of Anatomy & Physiology 12, Chemistry 12 or Physics 12; Chemistry 11; Physics 11) are applied as appropriate to international curricula.

requirements.notes: Standing in at least six academic subject areas with at least three academic A levels or six AS levels. UBC does not publish a fixed A-level grade or subject list.

subjects.subject: Chemistry or Physics (Grade 12 level) plus Grade 11-level Chemistry and Physics
subjects.notes: Mapped from UBC's Science prerequisites for Canadian applicants; UBC says these are applied as appropriate to international curricula.

requirements.notes: UBC publishes no fixed Indian-board subject list; assessed by UBC Admissions.

subjects.subject: Chemistry or Physics (Grade 12 level) plus Grade 11-level Chemistry and Physics

requirements.notes: Assessed by UBC Admissions; no fixed Indian-board subject list published.

subjects.subject: AP Chemistry (Chemistry 12), AP Physics 2 or C (Physics 12), AP Biology (Biology 12)
subjects.notes: Approved AP equivalents for Science prerequisites.

requirements.notes: Program-specific Science prerequisites for US applicants were not confirmed; check the calendar page.
